title: How do you hide the TP gauge from view until later in a given game?

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body:
Hello, all. Wanting to use TP for my summoning system, but summoning isn't an option until a little later in my game. Thus, I don't wish to have the TP gauge visible in menus--whether battle or elsewhere--until summoning becomes available--again, until a little later in my game. Otherwise players might wonder what the gauge is there for, why it's filling up, and all that kind of player confusion.
How would I go about doing this? Do I need a specific plugin to make this work? If so, which one, and what do I need to alter to make it work?
Thanks for reading!!

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
This should work.
Skill Core (YEP) - Yanfly.moe Wiki
www.yanfly.moe
I'm not 100% sure how to add back on but it shouldn't be that difficult.

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body: You could use skill core and give a state the notetage <swap 3: null> and give that state to the actor and then remove the state when you want tp to appear.

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body:
Thanks for these answers so far, you two!
Hmm. I must be doing something wrong. I believe I set the state correctly, adding the <swap 3: null> in the right notetag inside it. I then put the "Add State" to both party members who are at the beginning of the game. However, the TP bar still showed within the mock battle of sorts that happens during the beginning of the game.
Here are a pair of screens of what I have. Any guidance is most appreciated!

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body: My bad, I think it's supposed to be capitalized, <Swap Gauge 3: Null>

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body: There we go! Got it working so far. Thank you very much!

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body: All righty. I've stumbled upon an issue with my current setup. When a party member in battle gets K.O.'d, the TP gauge returns. How would I go about making that not happen? I could possibly put the null state on the K.O. notetag, but when I would want TP to be able to eventually get used, then the gauge would always disappear when a party member was K.O.'d.

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
Oh yeah, states are cleared on ko.
If you are using the steam version of rpg maker in the dlc folder that ships with rpg maker mv is a plugin called retain states on death or retain on death. It has a notetag to put on the state where it doesn't get cleared on ko.

posts.author: SuperPhillip
posts.body:
Yep! Have that DLC folder and plugin, so thanks for that! Found it with ease.
I definitely goofed something up in its implementation, though, because when I have the plugin ON, it causes the error in the first screenshot. I'm not sure what "push" is in this case or how I would go about defining it. I'm guessing this goes into Javascript territory, though, so this might make this thread off subject or in the wrong category perhaps. :x

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body: I don't think it likes battle core or buffs and states core. What's your plugin order look like? Try putting retainstateondeath below all yanfly plugins.
